answer: A lantern registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable stake in an onyx-hard escrow before it can trade, and it earns weight only through signed receipts for completed work. A newcomer arrives like a comet, bright but unproven, and must burn time and stake before its transactions carry full value. An attacker can mint a thousand identities, but each one needs its own stake, its own work history, and its own time, so cloning adds no power and the attack cost grows with every fake identity.
